data.narrative:
Quobly is a seed-stage quantum computing company founded by Maud Vinet, Tristan Meunier, and François Perruchot. The quantum computing sector comprises a comp universe of 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private firms, including later-stage peers such as Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable to Quobly. Despite 5 same-sector peers existing in the broader quantum computing landscape, zero companies meet the filtering criteria of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier, falling short of the minimum three datapoints required for reliable triangulation. An all-sector median approach would introduce substantial distortion given the stage and maturity dispersion within quantum computing.

The analysis cannot produce a specific valuation range at this time. The comp universe is populated but lacks sufficient same-stage or near-stage private comparables to anchor a quantitative estimate. Key uncertainties include Quobly's specific technical approach, IP position relative to named peers, capital efficiency trajectory, and commercial pathway within an emerging, heterogeneous sector. Progression to seed follow-on or Series A, accompanied by disclosed fundraising data and clearer technical differentiation, would enable meaningful peer triangulation. Current valuation work should rely on bottom-up cost-of-capital methods, management quality assessment, and scenario-based cash-flow modeling rather than comps-based approaches.
